blocks.en: Esther 8–10 — Deliverance, Conquest, and Purim
blocks.es_reference: Ester 8–10 — Liberación, conquista y Purim

blocks.en: Observations
blocks.es_reference: Observaciones

blocks.en: God's vengeance is perfect. Haman is hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai; Mordecai assumes Haman's place in royalty, even using the king's signet ring to sign a new decree; Mordecai gains all of Haman's estate; and the Jews annihilate those who wished to kill them, including Haman's ten sons. All the evil Haman planned comes back on him and his supporters.
blocks.es_reference: La venganza de Dios es perfecta. Amán es colgado en la horca que construyó para Mardoqueo; Mardoqueo asume el lugar de Amán en la realeza, usando incluso el anillo del rey para firmar un nuevo decreto; Mardoqueo recibe toda la hacienda de Amán; y los judíos aniquilan a quienes querían matarlos, incluidos los diez hijos de Amán. Todo el mal que Amán planeó recae sobre él y sus partidarios.

blocks.en: Notice Esther's address to the king on behalf of her people — she gives him deference, falling at his feet and weeping. Mordecai refused to bow to Haman, so they had no problem honoring those they felt deserved it.
blocks.es_reference: Note el modo en que Ester se dirige al rey a favor de su pueblo: le muestra deferencia, cayendo a sus pies y llorando. Mardoqueo se negó a inclinarse ante Amán, así que no tenían reparo en honrar a quienes sentían que lo merecían.

blocks.en: She says, 'If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor before him, and the matter seems proper to the king, and I am pleasing in his sight.' These phrases show her wisdom and her standing with her husband the king.
blocks.es_reference: Ella dice: “Si place al rey, y si he hallado gracia delante de él, y si la cosa es recta delante del rey, y si yo soy agradable a sus ojos.” Estas frases muestran su sabiduría y su posición ante su esposo el rey.

blocks.en: 8:11: the king granted the Jews the right to assemble and defend their lives, to destroy any force that might attack them, including that force's own children and women, and to plunder. The decree mirrors, almost word for word, the earlier decree against the Jews (3:13) — the sword Haman forged for the Jews is turned back on those who would wield it against them. It is a hard mercy to read, and honest interpreters have wrestled with it; the text does not soften it, and neither should we. Note the Jews were given permission to plunder — we'll return to that.
blocks.es_reference: 8:11: el rey concedió a los judíos el derecho de reunirse y defender sus vidas, de destruir toda fuerza que pudiera atacarlos, incluidos los propios niños y mujeres de esa fuerza, y de tomar botín. El decreto refleja, casi palabra por palabra, el decreto anterior contra los judíos (3:13) — la espada que Amán forjó para los judíos se vuelve contra quienes la esgrimirían contra ellos. Es un pasaje duro de leer, y intérpretes honestos lo han enfrentado con seriedad; el texto no lo suaviza, y nosotros tampoco debemos hacerlo. Note que a los judíos se les dio permiso de tomar botín; volveremos a eso.

blocks.en: As throughout the story, events come in pairs: for a second time Mordecai is arrayed as royalty, but now it becomes permanent.
blocks.es_reference: Como a lo largo de toda la historia, los acontecimientos vienen en pares: por segunda vez Mardoqueo es ataviado como realeza, pero ahora se vuelve permanente.

blocks.en: 8:17: 'There was gladness and joy for the Jews, a feast and a holiday. And many among the peoples of the land became Jews, for the dread of the Jews had fallen on them.' The 'dread' is really fear of the Jewish God who saves His people. They became proselytes hoping to gain that same protection.
blocks.es_reference: 8:17: “Los judíos tuvieron alegría y gozo, banquete y día de placer. Y muchos de entre los pueblos de la tierra se hacían judíos, porque el temor de los judíos había caído sobre ellos.” El “temor” es en realidad temor del Dios judío que salva a Su pueblo. Se hacían prosélitos esperando obtener esa misma protección.

blocks.en: Even the princes, satraps, and governors doing the king's business assisted the Jews.
blocks.es_reference: Incluso los príncipes, sátrapas y gobernadores que hacían los negocios del rey asistían a los judíos.

blocks.en: The dread of Mordecai: everyone in power now understands Mordecai the Jew is second only to the king.
blocks.es_reference: El temor de Mardoqueo: todos los que estaban en el poder ahora entienden que Mardoqueo el judío es segundo solo después del rey.

blocks.en: In Susa they kill 500 men, including Haman's sons — but they do not plunder. They only rid themselves of those who would kill them.
blocks.es_reference: En Susa matan a 500 hombres, incluidos los hijos de Amán, pero no toman botín. Solo se libran de quienes querían matarlos.

blocks.en: 9:13: Esther asks that the next day also be granted and that Haman's sons be hanged on the gallows — either another plot was uncovered or the work was unfinished; the hanged bodies stood as a warning. The next day they killed 300 more in the city, still without plundering.
blocks.es_reference: 9:13: Ester pide que también se conceda el día siguiente y que los hijos de Amán sean colgados en la horca; o bien se descubrió otro complot, o la obra estaba inconclusa; los cuerpos colgados servían de advertencia. Al día siguiente mataron a 300 más en la ciudad, todavía sin tomar botín.

blocks.en: In the provinces the Jews killed 75,000 — evidence of widespread anti-Semitism — but again they did not plunder.
blocks.es_reference: En las provincias los judíos mataron a 75,000, evidencia de un antisemitismo generalizado, pero de nuevo no tomaron botín.

blocks.en: The Jews celebrated on the 14th and 15th depending on where they lived, feasting, sending portions of food to one another, and giving gifts to the poor.
blocks.es_reference: Los judíos celebraron el día 14 y el 15, según donde vivían, festejando, enviándose porciones de comida unos a otros y dando regalos a los pobres.

blocks.en: Mordecai and Esther wrote to establish the holiday, called the command of Esther; it became a custom for them and their descendants and all allied with them — the Feast of Purim.
blocks.es_reference: Mardoqueo y Ester escribieron para establecer la festividad, llamada el mandato de Ester; se volvió costumbre para ellos y sus descendientes y todos los aliados con ellos: la Fiesta de Purim.

blocks.en: Pur became a symbol of God using circumstances to deliver His own — hence the disciples casting lots to replace Judas.
blocks.es_reference: Pur se volvió símbolo de Dios usando las circunstancias para librar a los suyos; de ahí que los discípulos echaran suertes para reemplazar a Judas.

blocks.en: Xerxes was an orthodox Zoroastrian — monotheistic with a dualistic good/evil system, a precursor to later religious intolerance. He destroyed Babylon's idol Bel Marduk, the god for which Mordecai is named. So for Esther to plead for her people twice was a huge risk.
blocks.es_reference: Jerjes era un zoroástrico ortodoxo —monoteísta con un sistema dualista de bien y mal, precursor de una posterior intolerancia religiosa—. Destruyó el ídolo de Babilonia, Bel Marduc, el dios por el cual Mardoqueo lleva su nombre. Así que para Ester interceder por su pueblo dos veces fue un riesgo enorme.

blocks.en: But Xerxes clearly loved Esther and would do anything for her. Mordecai and Esther elevated the status of being Jewish, because all had seen God's providence and salvation for the Jews.
blocks.es_reference: Pero Jerjes claramente amaba a Ester y haría cualquier cosa por ella. Mardoqueo y Ester elevaron el estatus de ser judío, porque todos habían visto la providencia y la salvación de Dios para los judíos.

blocks.en: Why would anyone still carry out the first decree after receiving the second? That is strong anti-Semitism indeed.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué llevaría alguien a cabo el primer decreto tras recibir el segundo? Eso sí es un antisemitismo fuerte.

blocks.en: Tom Constable notes: the absence of explicit reference to God helping His people does not deny His help; it reflects the attitude of Jews who ignored God's commands through Isaiah and Jeremiah to return to the land. They had pushed God aside, as Mordecai and Esther had to some extent — yet God remained faithful to His promises despite His people's unfaithfulness.
blocks.es_reference: Tom Constable observa: la ausencia de referencia explícita a Dios ayudando a Su pueblo no niega Su ayuda; refleja la actitud de los judíos que ignoraron los mandatos de Dios por medio de Isaías y Jeremías de volver a la tierra. Habían apartado a Dios, como Mardoqueo y Ester en cierta medida, y sin embargo Dios permaneció fiel a Sus promesas a pesar de la infidelidad de Su pueblo.

blocks.en: Interpretations
blocks.es_reference: Interpretaciones

blocks.en: Seldom do we get to see God's vengeance when we feel wronged. Usually life is more fluid, sticky, and ambiguous than a good story — especially for Christians, who are constantly self-examining and seeking the Spirit's guidance. Here the villain is readily exposed, right and wrong are mostly clear, and we see God's retribution on those who would harm His chosen people.
blocks.es_reference: Rara vez llegamos a ver la venganza de Dios cuando nos sentimos agraviados. Por lo general la vida es más fluida, enredada y ambigua que una buena historia, especialmente para los cristianos, que constantemente se autoexaminan y buscan la guía del Espíritu. Aquí el villano queda fácilmente expuesto, lo correcto y lo incorrecto están en su mayoría claros, y vemos la retribución de Dios sobre quienes querían dañar a Su pueblo escogido.

blocks.en: One of the most encouraging thoughts is that our salvation depends not on us but on a loving God who desires to save His children regardless of how badly we fail.
blocks.es_reference: Uno de los pensamientos más alentadores es que nuestra salvación no depende de nosotros, sino de un Dios amoroso que desea salvar a Sus hijos sin importar cuán gravemente fallemos.

blocks.en: That 'many became Jews' raises how we share the gospel today. We rarely see a complete reversal of evil, but there are everyday miracles. God reveals Himself today by our reflecting the light of Christ — loving others and proclaiming truth in kindness, gentleness, and love; entering the dark places of pain, poverty, injustice, sickness, and sin not to condemn but to share Christ's love; a community defined by self-sacrificial love.
blocks.es_reference: Que “muchos se hicieran judíos” plantea cómo compartimos el evangelio hoy. Rara vez vemos una reversión completa del mal, pero hay milagros cotidianos. Dios se revela hoy mediante nuestro reflejar la luz de Cristo: amando a otros y proclamando la verdad con bondad, mansedumbre y amor; entrando en los lugares oscuros de dolor, pobreza, injusticia, enfermedad y pecado no para condenar, sino para compartir el amor de Cristo; una comunidad definida por el amor que se sacrifica a sí mismo.

blocks.en: Remain upright in conduct — don't take the spoils. In everything we either glorify Christ or blaspheme His name; act accordingly with love.
blocks.es_reference: Permanezcamos rectos en la conducta: no tomemos el botín. En todo, o glorificamos a Cristo o blasfemamos Su nombre; obremos en consecuencia, con amor.

blocks.en: Let us not push God aside in our lives but keep Him our focus, and not quench the Holy Spirit within us.
blocks.es_reference: No apartemos a Dios de nuestra vida, sino mantengámoslo como nuestro enfoque, y no apaguemos al Espíritu Santo en nosotros.

blocks.en: Applications
blocks.es_reference: Aplicaciones

blocks.en: Are we truly a reflection of God's light? His love for people was beautiful and ever-present, but so was His truth — He always spoke the truth in love, and many turned away. We should expect no different. People will know we are Christians by our love, but love alone is not the whole of it.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Somos verdaderamente un reflejo de la luz de Dios? Su amor por las personas era hermoso y siempre presente, pero también lo era Su verdad: siempre habló la verdad en amor, y muchos se apartaron. No deberíamos esperar nada distinto. La gente sabrá que somos cristianos por nuestro amor, pero el amor por sí solo no es la totalidad.

blocks.en: Am I prepared to share my testimony of what Christ has done in my life?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Estoy preparado para compartir mi testimonio de lo que Cristo ha hecho en mi vida?

mc.stem: After Haman's death, Mordecai is given:
options: the king's signet ring and Haman's estate
mc.why: He receives the signet ring and Haman's whole estate.

mc.stem: Glenda calls the reversal of Haman's evil onto himself an example of:
mc.why: The evil he planned recoils on him — God's justice.

mc.stem: Approaching the king again, Esther shows deference by:
options: falling at his feet and weeping
mc.why: She falls at his feet weeping — honoring whom she should.

mc.stem: In the new decree, the phrase authorizing the Jews to destroy an attacking force ‘including children and women’ refers to:
options: the attacking force's own children and women, mirroring Haman's original decree
the Jewish children and women from the first edict
mc.why: The decree grants the Jews the same terms Haman's decree had granted their enemies (3:13) — authority to destroy an attacking force including its own women and children. It is a sobering mirror-image reversal, not a protection clause for Jewish families.

mc.stem: A striking, repeated feature Glenda notes is that the Jews:
options: did NOT take the plunder, though permitted
mc.why: Though allowed to plunder, they refused it — three times noted.

mc.stem: Esther 8:17 says many people of the land 'became Jews' because:
options: the dread of the Jews (really their God) had fallen on them
mc.why: Dread of the Jews' God drew them to become proselytes.

mc.stem: In Susa the Jews killed 500 men plus Haman's sons; notably they:
mc.why: They only removed those who would kill them — no plunder.

mc.stem: Why were Haman's already-dead sons hanged on the gallows?
options: as a strong public warning against attacking the Jews
mc.why: Their hung bodies warned any who would attack the Jews.

mc.stem: In the provinces the Jews killed how many of their enemies?
mc.why: 75,000 — showing the scale of those identified as enemies of the Jews in the narrative.

mc.stem: The two days of celebration were marked by feasting and:
options: sending food to one another and gifts to the poor
mc.why: Feasting, sharing food, and gifts to the poor.

mc.stem: The festival Mordecai and Esther established is called:
mc.why: Purim, named from 'pur' (the lot).

mc.stem: The name 'Purim' derives from 'pur,' which became a symbol of:
options: God using circumstances to deliver His own
mc.why: Pur — lot — became a symbol of God's delivering providence.

mc.stem: Glenda notes the disciples later cast lots (pur-like) to:
mc.why: They cast lots to replace Judas, trusting God's choice.

mc.stem: King Xerxes' religion is identified by Glenda as:
mc.why: Ancient Persian religion is debated by scholars, but Xerxes is widely thought to have been Zoroastrian.

mc.stem: Ironically, Xerxes had destroyed Babylon's idol Bel Marduk — the god for whom:
mc.why: Mordecai's name derives from Marduk; ancient sources describe Xerxes acting against the Marduk cult, though details are debated — a quiet irony.

mc.stem: Esther pleading for her people twice was a huge risk especially because the king:
mc.why: His religious intolerance made her double plea risky.

mc.stem: By the end, the 'dread of Mordecai' means everyone in power understands he is:
mc.why: Mordecai is now second only to the king.

mc.stem: Tom Constable explains the absence of explicit reference to God's help reflects:
options: the Jews having pushed God aside by not returning to the land
mc.why: It mirrors Jews who'd sidelined God, who stayed faithful anyway.

mc.stem: Glenda's conclusion is that our salvation ultimately depends on:
options: a loving God who saves regardless of how we fail
mc.why: God saves out of love, despite our failures.

mc.stem: Glenda's closing application is that we are to be a community defined by:
options: self-sacrificial love that speaks truth in love
mc.why: Self-sacrificial love, truth spoken in love.

sa.prompt: How is God's perfect justice displayed in the reversal of Haman's plans?
sa.model: Haman is hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai; Mordecai takes Haman's royal place, signet ring, and estate; and the Jews defeat those who sought their destruction, including Haman's ten sons. All the evil Haman devised recoils on him — God's perfect vengeance.

sa.prompt: Why does Glenda emphasize that the Jews did not take the plunder?
sa.model: Though the decree permitted plundering, three times the text notes they did not. They only removed those who would kill them, keeping their conduct upright — a reminder that in all we do we either glorify Christ or blaspheme His name.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of many people 'becoming Jews' (Esther 8:17)?
sa.model: The dread that fell on the peoples was really fear of the Jews' God, who always saves His people. They became proselytes hoping for that same protection — a picture of how witness can draw others to God.

sa.prompt: Describe the establishment and meaning of the Feast of Purim.
sa.model: Mordecai and Esther wrote to fix the 14th and 15th as days of feasting, sending food to one another, and giving gifts to the poor. Called the command of Esther, it became Purim — named from 'pur,' the lot — a lasting symbol of God using circumstances to deliver His own.

sa.prompt: What irony does Glenda note about Xerxes' religion and Mordecai's name?
sa.model: Xerxes is widely thought to have been an intolerant orthodox Zoroastrian, and ancient sources describe him acting against Babylon's cult of Bel Marduk, though the precise details are debated — the very god for whom Mordecai was named. That intolerance made Esther's twofold plea for her people an especially grave risk.

sa.prompt: How does Tom Constable explain God's apparent absence in the book?
sa.model: Constable says the lack of explicit reference to God's help does not deny it; it reflects the attitude of Jews who ignored God's commands through Isaiah and Jeremiah to return to the land, having pushed God aside — yet God stayed faithful to His promises despite their unfaithfulness.

sa.prompt: What does the conquest reveal about the depth of anti-Semitism in the empire?
sa.model: That 75,000 enemies in the provinces still moved to attack even after the second decree shows the scale of those identified as enemies of the Jews in the narrative — people pressing on with the first decree's murderous intent despite the reversal; describing this fully with the modern term anti-Semitism requires some care, since the text frames it in terms of political enmity following the first decree.

sa.prompt: How does Glenda apply 'many became Jews' to our witness today?
sa.model: We rarely see a dramatic reversal of evil today, but God reveals Himself as we reflect Christ's light — loving others and proclaiming truth in kindness and gentleness, entering the dark places of pain and injustice not to condemn but to share His love as a self-sacrificial community.

sa.prompt: What lesson about God's salvation does Glenda draw from the book's conclusion?
sa.model: Our salvation depends not on us but on a loving God who desires to save His children regardless of how badly they fail — just as He saved a disobedient, God-sidelining people through Esther and Mordecai by His faithful providence.

sa.prompt: Summarize Glenda's final challenge about reflecting God's light and truth.
sa.model: We are to reflect God's light by both love and truth, as Christ always spoke truth in love though many turned away. People should know us by our love, but love alone is not enough; we must also be prepared to share our testimony of what Christ has done in us.
